shoreditch.name: Shoreditch
shoreditch.blurb: Home turf. Rents keep going up and nobody knows why. No ore runs stronger than the rest here — you take whatever surfaces.

city.name: The City
city.blurb: Every building is a bank, a firm, or both, and something older underneath. Fate ore turns up more than anything else; the City's always been in the business of who owes what to whom.

greenwich.name: Greenwich
greenwich.blurb: The Meridian runs through it, which the locals will mention unprompted. Time ore turns up here more than anywhere else in London.

camden.name: Camden
camden.blurb: Markets, market stalls, and men who are technically also a market stall. Physics ore is most of what comes up — nothing here holds still long enough to settle.

kingscross.name: King's Cross
kingscross.special: veins here: +1 rightward drift, -1 leftward drift (min 0)
kingscross.blurb: Everything in King's Cross is on its way somewhere else. Even the veins grow faster, and what surfaces leans time and physics in roughly equal measure.

battersea.name: Battersea
battersea.blurb: The power station stopped generating decades ago. Something still hums. Physics ore is most of what turns up — the old cooling towers never really switched off.

hampstead.name: Hampstead
hampstead.blurb: Old money and older trees. The Heath keeps its own counsel, and what grows under it is mostly life ore.

whitechapel.name: Whitechapel
whitechapel.special: vein NPC-raid chance ×1.5 (when vein raids land, M2)
whitechapel.blurb: The oldest grief in London, still paying rent to the newest landlords. Emotion ore is most of what surfaces — grief doesn't decompose round here, it just changes hands.

soho.name: Soho
soho.blurb: Nothing grows here — no sites, no veins, nothing to prospect. Everything gets sold here eventually.

nottinghill.name: Notting Hill
nottinghill.blurb: Pastel terraces and a carnival that never quite leaves. Emotion ore is most of what surfaces — a district built on being looked at tends to feel everything twice.

kensington.name: Kensington
kensington.blurb: Museums full of things nobody asked to have kept. Time and fate ore turn up in roughly equal measure; the collections have never been properly audited.

chelsea.name: Chelsea
chelsea.blurb: Money here is polite about itself. Fate ore is most of what comes up — the King's Road has always known who owes whom, and mostly declines to say.

hammersmith.name: Hammersmith
hammersmith.blurb: The flyover shakes the flats and the flats have stopped noticing. Physics and emotion ore split most of what surfaces, usually the same night as a gig.

clapham.name: Clapham
clapham.blurb: The Common is always full of someone's weekend. Life and emotion ore surface in about equal measure — brunch is a kind of grief, if you stay long enough.
